criteria.rationale: Examined the fix, the gitCommandContext environment build and every snapshotGit caller. Verified: the env is preserved (git_snapshot_integrity.go:576-583, var appended at :113), all snapshotGit callers are covered, and no caller depends on index refresh. Unresolved: submodule children inherit GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS (reasoned from Git's behaviour, not tested); the test failing without the variable was not re-run by me; R2 is a manual harne8 measurement; artifact-check reports head 6e27b06d vs brief 4cc3b954. Accepted: F1, F2 (low).
No shared state, goroutines or lifecycle changed; the fix removes a concurrent writer (index.lock) under .git, which reduces contention with governed read views and other git processes.
Arguments, porcelain -z parsing and the GitSnapshotError type are unchanged; only the subprocess environment differs.
Error path unchanged: failures still return a typed GitSnapshotError naming the operation (git_snapshot_integrity.go:115-117).
snapshotGit consumers (review_dispatch, review_attempt_ledger, review_adapter_containment, ReadGitStatusIn) parse output only; their sealed integration checks pass.
Diagnostics unchanged: GitSnapshotError still carries the operation and cause; the fix removes a false 'review inputs changed during operation: .git' diagnosis.
Examined the CLI/MCP/file surfaces: no contract changes; git status output with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 is identical, only the opportunistic index write is skipped. Concluded compatible.
The test makes the stat cache stale with identical content (the exact trigger for git's optional index refresh) and asserts the index is byte-identical and no index.lock remains.

Examined D1 against R1: the cause (git status rewriting .git/index via index.lock under a read view watching .git) is removed at its source, matching the policy of the governed executors (governance_read_view_git.go:601, operation_git.go:26). The rejected alternative, filtering .git from observation, would hide real writes. Concluded the design addresses the cause.
Examined the changelog entry, spec and in-code comment at git_snapshot_integrity.go:110-112; they match runtime behaviour. No operational docs or templates are affected.
Examined the error paths: unchanged and typed. The fix eliminates a spurious, non-actionable closeout error (60 in harne8 per the spec).

Examined the diff against the spec's artifact list: the Go change, test, start, changelog and matrix entry are as declared. The derived indexes are regenerated administrative files; artifact-check reports no error for this change. Concluded in scope.
Examined the env handling: gitRedirectingEnv filtering and replace/graft hardening are preserved because the variable is appended after them. No new inputs, paths or authority. Concluded safe.

Compared with the smallest alternative: a one-line env change plus one test is the minimum; there is no speculative extensibility. Invalidating condition: a snapshot git command that still writes under .git (D1's falsifier) or other executors on the read path lacking the variable (F2).
